title: Kerala Dayz: A Taxi and Tour Website Built to Book in One Tap
storyLead: How Teknoppy designed and developed a fast Astro website for a Kochi taxi operator, with a map-based booking form, fleet rates and WhatsApp booking for airport, outstation and tour trips.
location: Athani, near Cochin International Airport, Nedumbassery, Kochi, Kerala
services: UX and UI design, Astro development, booking form and map picker, content structure, on-page SEO
atAGlance: Teknoppy designed and developed keraladayz.com, the website of Kerala Dayz, a chauffeur-driven taxi and tour operator in Athani near Cochin International Airport, running since 2008
Built with the Astro framework, the site has a booking form with a map-based location picker
Fleet cards show rates and WhatsApp links, alongside service and destination pages, tour packages, reviews and a 24/7 contact flow
Kerala Dayz' own published figures: 4.9/5 from 1,359 Google reviews, 10,000+ travellers served, 50+ verified drivers, in business since 2008
aboutParagraphs: Travellers landing at Cochin airport, families planning a Munnar trip and pilgrims heading to Sabarimala all want the same thing: a safe, fairly priced taxi booked in minutes. Kerala Dayz needed a website that proves it is trustworthy and makes booking almost effortless on a phone.

Kerala Dayz was founded in 2008 by Antony Liston, an approved Incredible India Tourist Facilitator. It runs airport taxi, outstation and one-way trips, pilgrim taxi, corporate and wedding taxi, car rental with driver and tour packages.

Its fleet includes sedans, family SUVs, Innova Crysta, Tempo Traveller, a luxury coach and a 35-seater AC bus, covering Kochi, Munnar, Alleppey, Thekkady, Wayanad, Kumarakom, Varkala, Kovalam and more, plus Tamil Nadu and Karnataka.
challengeLead: Three problems shaped the design brief.

challenges.title: Booking a taxi must take seconds
challenges.description: Many visitors are standing at an airport or planning on the move. Long forms or unclear pickup points send them to an app or a rival operator.

challenges.title: Price and safety worries
challenges.description: Tourists fear hidden charges and unknown drivers. The site had to show fixed fares, driver vetting and real credentials before asking for a booking.

challenges.title: A wide range of trips and vehicles
challenges.description: Airport drops, multi-day tours, pilgrim routes, weddings and 35-seater buses all need to be easy to find without making the site feel cluttered.

objectiveLead: The goal was a taxi website built for speed, trust and one-tap booking.
objectives: Fast booking: let guests book with a few taps, even on slow mobile data
Clear prices: show fleet rates and what is included before the booking
Proof of trust: put ratings, credentials and driver vetting up front
Easy discovery: organise services, fleet, destinations and packages so every trip has a page
approachLead: How Teknoppy ran the project, designed the site and developed it.

approachPillars.title: Our process
paragraphs: 1. Discovery: Mapped traveller types, trip types, fleet and booking steps with the Kerala Dayz team
2. Sitemap: Planned service, fleet, destination, route and package pages with a mega menu
3. UI/UX design: Designed a green, card-based layout with the booking form in the hero
4. Development: Built the site in Astro with the booking form, map picker and carousels
5. Content: Added fleet rates, credentials, packages, FAQs and blog posts
6. Testing and launch: Tested forms, map picker, WhatsApp links and mobile layouts

approachPillars.title: Booking in the hero
paragraphs: The hero pairs a headline and vehicle photo with a quick booking form, so guests can start booking the moment the page loads. "Book a Taxi" also stays in the header.

approachPillars.title: Trust before the ask
paragraphs: An accreditation strip shows Tripadvisor, Ministry of Tourism, KRT and Google rating badges right under the hero, followed by six feature points on verified drivers, fixed pricing and 24/7 support.

approachPillars.title: Fleet cards that sell
paragraphs: Six fleet cards show each vehicle with its rate details and a WhatsApp booking link, so guests can compare and book the right car in one step.

approachPillars.title: Every trip has a place
paragraphs: Service cards, seven destination cards, three tour packages, a four-step "How Booking Works" section and an internal link directory for cities and routes help guests find exactly what they need.

approachPillars.title: Design decisions that mattered most
paragraphs: Booking form inside the hero: Visitors ready to book never have to scroll or search
Map picker for pickup points: Exact locations mean fewer calls and missed pickups
Rates shown on every fleet card: Clear prices remove the fear of hidden charges
Credentials right under the hero: Trust is built before the booking is asked for
WhatsApp as the confirmation step: Most Kerala travellers already use it every day

approachPillars.title: How Teknoppy developed the website
paragraphs: We chose the Astro framework because it sends very little JavaScript to the browser. Pages load fast on mobile data, which matters for travellers checking the site at an airport or on the road.
Booking form: Name, pickup and drop, dates, passengers and vehicle type, with required-field validation
Map location picker: Modal map with search and popular-location shortcuts for exact pickup points
WhatsApp booking: Prefilled WhatsApp messages from the form and every fleet card
Page transitions: Astro view transitions for smooth movement between pages
Media: Review carousel, photo gallery and embedded videos
SEO setup: Keyword-led title and meta, canonical tag, Open Graph and Twitter cards, internal link directory

deliverables.title: Hero booking form + map picker
deliverables.description: Book with an exact pickup point in seconds.

deliverables.title: Fleet cards with rates
deliverables.description: Compare cars and prices before booking.

deliverables.title: City, route and service links
deliverables.description: Every trip type has its own page.

whyMattersParagraphs: We judge the site by bookings, not just visits. The numbers tracked each month are booking form submissions, WhatsApp chats, calls to the 24/7 line, mobile page speed, and which services and routes bring the most bookings.

Next for the website: match passenger numbers on fleet cards and the booking form, remove repeated reviews and the duplicate rate note, use one name for each vehicle model across the site, and add online payment for advance booking.
whyMattersCalloutHtml:
Key takeaways: put the booking form where the visitor lands, show the price and the proof before the ask, let WhatsApp do the confirming, and build on a fast framework.

faqs.question: What should a taxi service website include?
faqs.answer: A quick booking form, fleet with prices, services and routes, reviews, credentials, a clear contact line and WhatsApp booking.

faqs.question: Why add a map location picker to a booking form?
faqs.answer: It lets guests set an exact pickup point, which reduces calls and missed pickups, especially for hotels and homes.

faqs.question: Why build a travel website with Astro?
faqs.answer: Astro sends very little JavaScript, so pages load fast. Speed keeps mobile visitors on the page and helps rankings.

faqs.question: Can bookings be confirmed on WhatsApp?
faqs.answer: Yes. The booking form and fleet cards open WhatsApp with the trip details filled in, so confirmation takes one tap.

faqs.question: How long does a travel website project take?
faqs.answer: It depends on pages, booking features and content. Teknoppy gives a written timeline and fixed quote after a free consultation.

faqs.question: Does Teknoppy build websites for travel and taxi businesses?
faqs.answer: Yes. Teknoppy is a web design and development company in Kochi, Kerala, building websites for taxi operators, tour companies, resorts and businesses across Kerala and the GCC.
